messages:
Maya (PM): quick sync — proposing a small schedule reset for the launch. ran the numbers, we can either keep date and cut feature set A, or move GA by 3 weeks to keep A + B. thoughts?
Jin (Eng): what exactly is in feature set A vs B?
Maya (PM): A = tenant routing, SSO scaffolding, basic telemetry. B = embeddings cache, rate-limit per-tenant, and nicer error surfaces.
Priya (Design): from UX POV embeddings cache improvements are polish, not blocking. SSO + routing are must-haves for enterprise pilot.
Sam (Customer PM): our pilot customer (Acme) cares mainly about SSO + routing and telemetry for compliance. embeddings are low priority for them.
Jin (Eng): baseline engineering estimate: A only -> keep date but we need to cut some non-blocking infra work (observability extras). A+B -> +3 weeks, lower risk to oncall.
Alex (SRE): if we keep date and cut infra extras, ops runbook gaps remain. We can put mitigations: increase paging window, add temporary dashboards. Not ideal but doable.
Liza (VP Product): prefer to keep commitment to customers. If key customers need SSO+routing, we must ensure that's solid. Can we scope an intermediate approach?
Maya (PM): proposal: keep GA date but formally de-scope 'embeddings cache' and 'per-tenant rate-limit' for GA; add them to v1 (ship +3w). That keeps enterprise asks satisfied. Decision call?
Jin (Eng): ok but we need a firm cut list. I suggest de-scope: embeddings cache (B1), nice error surfaces (B2), async batch optimizer (B3). Keep SSO, routing, telemetry.
Priya (Design): agree — UX for errors can be simplified to generic modal and addressed in v1.
Sam (Customer PM): confirm with Acme — they accept embeddings later as long as SSO & telemetry land in GA. I'll ping them now.
Maya (PM): Sam please confirm before EOD. If yes, we lock cut list and keep GA. Otherwise we push 3 weeks.
launch-bot: Reminder: Feature-freeze scheduled for 1802190000 (in ~16 hours)
Jin (Eng): technical risk notes: SSO includes scim mapping edge-case that may take 2 dev days if customer has odd groups. We should flag as risk and add test plan.
Alex (SRE): Ops prep: need an additional runbook section for tenant routing fallback. I can write a draft in 1 day if cuts confirmed.
Maya (PM): Action items: 1) Sam confirm Acme acceptance (owner: Sam) 2) Jin & Alex produce final risk log & mitigations (owner: Jin/Alex) 3) Priya create simplified error flows (owner: Priya) 4) Maya update roadmap and release notes (owner: Maya).
Priya (Design): ETA for simplified flows: tomorrow morning.
Jin (Eng): risk log done by EOD.
Sam (Customer PM): pinged Acme — they said fine to postpone embeddings but asked for a telemetry contract (SLA on retention & export).
Maya (PM): noted. Jin — can we commit to telemetry export (S3) for GA?
Jin (Eng): yes, core telemetry export to S3 is straightforward. Will scope it into A.
Liza (VP Product): decision: lock cut list as Maya proposed. Keep GA date. Official note: de-scope B features (embeddings cache, per-tenant rate-limits, nice error surfaces). Move to v1.
Maya (PM): logging decision here so we have a record. I'll update the public roadmap and notify sales.
Sam (Customer PM): Acme confirmed in-writing. will attach email to the ticket.
Alex (SRE): started runbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RD-4567 - will add fallback steps.
Jin (Eng): I'll push a short config flag so we can toggle routing fallback during rollout.
Maya (PM): final check — do we need to move QA cycles? can we still finish acceptance testing by freeze?
Priya (Design): QA for simplified error flows is smaller — should be fine.
Jin (Eng): QA: need 3x test passes for SSO across 2 tenants + routing smoke. We can hit that before freeze if no blockers.
Maya (PM): ok good. I'll run a pre-freeze check-in tomorrow 10am.
Liza (VP Product): thanks team. keep everything in the release ticket and flag any slippage ASAP. :thumbsup:
Maya (PM): closing thread — cut list locked, GA date maintained. I'll post updated release notes in #release-war-room after the check-in.
launch-bot: Note: Freeze will be enforced at 1802190000 unless release-owner sets an exemption.
